top_signals.title: Oil Prices Rebound Sharply After Brutal Midweek Rout
top_signals.summary: Oil prices surged Thursday, recovering some of Wednesday's staggering losses as traders reconsidered whether the U.S. midterm election results would actually bring a swift end to the Iran war. Brent crude had climbed to $98.01 per barrel by early afternoon, gaining $3.39, or 3.58%, while West Texas Intermediate rose $2.21, or 2.51%, to $90.33. Both benchmarks continued climbing later in the session. The rebound followed Wednesday's extraordinary selloff, when Brent plunged $8.98, or 8.7%, to settle at $94.62. top_signals.title: China’s 10-Year Yield Hits Record Intraday Low on Haven Demand
top_signals.summary: China’s benchmark 10-year sovereign yield dropped to an all-time intraday low, driven by haven demand and a recent shift in the policy rate that was regarded as a de facto easing.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Mystery Seller Puts Up $500 Million Data Center Loans Backing Stargate, CyrusOne
top_signals.summary: Dutch bank ING is putting up for sale a roughly $500 million portfolio of data center loans all at once, according to people familiar with the matter. The rare auction comes just days after a Democratic sweep of the US midterm elections raised doubts about the future of many of the projects.
